earliest_visible_sign.description: Tiny yellow or pale chlorotic flecks or small oval water-soaked spots.

characteristic_sign_or_lesion.description: Small diamond-shaped lesions that elongate with age, eventually becoming elongated rectangular lesions constrained by adjacent leaf veins.

colors.color_progression: yellow/pale tan to light brown centre with reddish-brown to dark brown margin

shape.shape_progression: small diamond-shaped lesions that elongate with age to become elongated rectangular lesions constrained by adjacent leaf veins

size.size_variation_note: Lesion size and shape vary with the pathogen race, maize genotype, and disease severity.

texture_and_surface.sporulation_or_sign: dark grey or black when sporulating/rotting

border_and_margin.halo: chlorotic halos may be present in certain races (e.g. Race T)

advanced_or_severe_stage.description: Coalescing lesions form large brown necrotic areas resulting in premature drying and complete foliage blight.
advanced_or_severe_stage.coalescence: Lesions merge, producing extensive necrosis, premature leaf death, and whole-leaf blighting.
advanced_or_severe_stage.tissue_death_appearance: large brown necrotic areas, premature drying and death of leaves
secondary_signs: black or dark mould on affected silks, husks, cobs, or kernels
advanced_or_severe_stage.percentage_affected_tissue_note: complete foliage blight in severe infections

distribution_on_plant.vertical_pattern: usually begins on lower leaves and increases upward through the canopy
distribution_on_plant.horizontal_pattern: lesions initially remain between veins and later merge
distribution_on_plant.other_parts_if_severe: husks, silks, ears, cobs, and kernels

pathognomonic_features: Elongated rectangular lesions with tan/light-brown centres and reddish-brown/dark-brown margins, strongly constrained by adjacent leaf veins.
Early stage features distinctive small diamond-shaped lesions.
